releases.title: Portable Flashing Package: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.7
releases.source_notes:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.7: Bluetooth rebuilt for reliability.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → System → Software Update → **Update Now** (on Beta 9.2.8 and older: Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**).

## What changed
Bluetooth used to be handled by five separate pieces that coordinated through lock files; when two acted at once, headphones stayed half connected or reconnects stalled. One radio program now owns Bluetooth and the radio it shares with Wi-Fi. The player says what it wants, and the radio program gets there and repairs itself. Every codec, rate and quality setting from 9.2.16 is kept.

- **Headphones come back after sleep**, also when they reconnect by themselves: AirPods Pro were ready 2.5–5 s after a wake (before: often 15–20 s).
- **Bluetooth repairs itself** (cancel a stuck step, restart the radio, BlueALSA, BlueZ). If everything fails it says so: switching Bluetooth off and on in Settings now restarts all of Bluetooth.
- **Connect Automatically per device** (Y2Reborn #78): Settings → Bluetooth → a paired device.
- **Codec and quality changes apply without restarting the player** (the headphones are back in about 7–9 s).
- **Your library is no longer emptied when a Bluetooth output fails** (Y2Reborn #92).
- Headphones that are switched off are no longer paged forever; pausing keeps the connection instead of stopping the stream; Wi-Fi uses its power saving while Bluetooth plays; after sleep Wi-Fi waits for your headphones; each pair of headphones starts at the rate it managed last time.

Before release: the platform's full check, Reborn's workspace tests, the 552 tests of the release images, and a fake Bluetooth stack with six failure scenarios. On the developer's player with AirPods Pro: 19 sleep/wake cycles without a failed connection. Only AirPods Pro were tried, and there is no overnight run on this exact build yet: if your headphones behave worse than in 9.2.16, please send an error report.

What changed and why, in plain words: **[Beta 9.3.7 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.3.7.md)**. Versions 9.3 to 9.3.6 were unpublished test builds; everything from Beta 9.2.16 is included ([Beta 9.2.16 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.2.16.md)).

## Install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.9.3.7-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: the player sets up its Internal Storage (a few seconds), then Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

Full guide: [INSTALL](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) · How updates work: [Recovery and updates](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/RECOVERY-AND-UPDATES.md) · Storage: [Storage](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/STORAGE.md) · [Audiobooks](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/AUDIOBOOKS.md) · Headphone settings: [Headphone output](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/HEADPHONE-OUTPUT.md) · [Error reports](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/ERROR-REPORTS.md) · Skins: [skin guide](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Reborn/blob/main/docs/skins.md)

## Known issues (beta)
- **Bluetooth after a long pause:** with AirPods Pro, a pause longer than about 20 seconds drops the connection once; they reconnect within seconds, but pressing play during those 20 seconds can stay silent until they are back. Being investigated.
- Everything listed for Beta 9.0 still applies. If anything behaves differently from 9.2.16, send an error report (Settings → System → Error Reports); **Restore Previous System** (Settings → System → About, tap Version seven times, then Diagnostics) goes back to the version you had, with your data kept.
- Battery life in sleep: about 2 mA overnight on the developer's player (estimated from the battery voltage); stock is about 1.3 mA.
- Some players turned off by themselves during playback; the cause is not found yet. If yours does, start it again and send a report.
- The speaker uses the same volume as the headphones; its loudest step is the stock speaker's. Start low the first time.
- How loud the wheel click should be is a first guess; tell us if it is too loud or too soft.
- BBC radio stations stream only in HLS, which the player does not play yet. FM radio is in the works for a later beta.

**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.2.13: one song from search, quick audiobook resume, letter scrolling you can reach.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → System → Software Update → **Update Now** (on Beta 9.2.8 and older: Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**).

## What changed
- **One song from search** (Y2Reborn #79): picking a song in the search results played every song found. Now it plays just that song; **Play All** plays them all.
- **Long MP3 and AAC files continue at once** (Y2Reborn #80): after the player had slept, audiobooks and long recordings in these formats took seconds to continue, longer the further in you were, because the player read the file from the start to find your place. It now remembers the places it passed and starts just before yours (the first resume after a restart still reads once). M4A, M4B and Opus were never affected.
- **Letter scrolling you can reach** (Y2Linux #64): since 9.2.2 the letter jumps needed the wheel's very fastest speed, which a hard spin did not reach. They start at a real spin again; a quick, steady turn still moves row by row.
- **Why Bluetooth disconnected:** error reports now say whether the link was lost, the headphones ended it or the player did. If your headphones drop often, send a report right after it happens (Settings → System → Error Reports).

Before release: the platform's full check, Reborn's workspace tests (new, each failing without its change: one song from search; a reopened AAC file lands on its place without reading from the start; letter scrolling at a spin; Bluetooth disconnect reasons) and the tests of the release images. Still to check on a player: resume time after sleep and how the letter speed feels.

What changed and why, in plain words: **[Beta 9.2.13 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.2.13.md)**. Everything from Beta 9.2.12 is included ([Beta 9.2.12 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.2.12.md)).

## Install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.9.2.13-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: the player sets up its Internal Storage (a few seconds), then Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

Full guide: [INSTALL](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) · How updates work: [Recovery and updates](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/RECOVERY-AND-UPDATES.md) · Storage: [Storage](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/STORAGE.md) · [Audiobooks](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/AUDIOBOOKS.md) · Headphone settings: [Headphone output](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/HEADPHONE-OUTPUT.md) · [Error reports](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/ERROR-REPORTS.md) · Skins: [skin guide](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Reborn/blob/main/docs/skins.md)

## Known issues (beta)
- Everything listed for Beta 9.0 still applies. If anything behaves differently from 9.2.12, send an error report (Settings → System → Error Reports); **Restore Previous System** (Settings → System → About, tap Version seven times, then Diagnostics) goes back to the version you had, with your data kept.
- Battery life in sleep: about 2 mA overnight on the developer's player (estimated from the battery voltage); stock is about 1.3 mA.
- Some players turned off by themselves during playback; the cause is not found yet. If yours does, start it again and send a report.
- The speaker uses the same volume as the headphones; its loudest step is the stock speaker's. Start low the first time.
- How loud the wheel click should be is a first guess; tell us if it is too loud or too soft.

**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.2.8: why a Wi-Fi router turns the player away.** Linux 6.18 and the native Reborn music player for the Innioasis Y2.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

## What changed
- **Wi-Fi refusals are recorded** (#83): when a router refuses to let the player join, error reports now note the reason each refusal gave (or that the router never answered), so we can tell a router that turns the Y2 away on purpose from one that does not hear it. Nothing you will see changes.
- If your player keeps failing to join your Wi-Fi, send an error report right after it happens. Routers that use one name for 2.4 and 5 GHz ("band steering", "Smart Connect") may push devices to 5 GHz, which the Y2 does not have; a separate 2.4 GHz network is worth a try.

Tested on the developer's player: installed over the air from Beta 9.2.7 and confirmed by the player itself; all services and Reborn running, health OK. Before release: the platform's full check, Reborn's workspace tests and the tests of the release images.

What changed and why, in plain words: **[Beta 9.2.8 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.2.8.md)**. Everything from Beta 9.2.7 is included ([Beta 9.2.7 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.2.7.md)).

## Install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.9.2.8-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: the player sets up its Internal Storage (a few seconds), then Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

Full guide: [INSTALL](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) · How updates work: [Recovery and updates](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/RECOVERY-AND-UPDATES.md) · Storage: [Storage](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/STORAGE.md) · [Audiobooks](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/AUDIOBOOKS.md) · Headphone settings: [Headphone output](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/HEADPHONE-OUTPUT.md) · [Error reports](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/ERROR-REPORTS.md) · Skins: [skin guide](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Reborn/blob/main/docs/skins.md)

- Everything listed for Beta 9.0 still applies. If anything behaves differently from 9.2.7, send an error report (Settings → Diagnostics); Settings → Diagnostics → **Restore Previous System** goes back to the version you had, with your data kept.
- Battery life in sleep: about 2 mA overnight on the developer's player (estimated from the battery voltage); stock is about 1.3 mA.
- Some players turned off by themselves during playback; the cause is not found yet. If yours does, start it again and send a report.
- The speaker uses the same volume as the headphones; its loudest step is the stock speaker's. Start low the first time.
- How loud the wheel click should be is a first guess; tell us if it is too loud or too soft.
- BBC radio stations stream only in HLS, which the player does not play yet. FM radio is in the works for a later beta.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.

Beta 9.0 looks and works like Beta 8.43. Your music, playlists, play queue, settings, Wi-Fi networks, Bluetooth pairings and Last.fm sign-in all stay. What changed is everything **underneath** the music player. This is the biggest change to Y2Linux since the first beta.

### The part you never see: "the platform"
The Y2 runs two kinds of software. **Reborn** is the music player you see: the menus, Now Playing, the library and the settings screens. Underneath it, **the platform** works all the time: four small background services and one command tool. Between them they:
- watch the battery and switch the player off safely before it runs flat;
- put the player to sleep and wake it, and check afterwards that it really slept and woke on the same start;
- connect and supervise Wi-Fi, keep the clock right, and turn Bluetooth on and off;
- check SD cards before they are used, keep a healthy card read-only between writes so pulling it out can't damage it, and repair or format a card when you ask;
- set up Internal Storage on the first start;
- download, verify and install updates, and undo an update that doesn't start properly;
- show your music to a computer over USB;
- collect and send error reports when you choose to.

Every time Reborn shows the battery, the Wi-Fi state, the storage page or the update page, it asks the platform.

### From Python to Rust
Until 8.43 the platform was written in **Python**, which needs its own interpreter on the player. That had costs you could feel:
- **Every question took about half a second.** Each request started a new Python program, even "is the player asleep?". Reborn asks every few seconds while the screen is on, and so do the Wi-Fi and clock events and every start and shutdown step.
- **CPU time is battery.** While the player was on but idle, the platform alone used about 92 CPU seconds every hour.
- **Memory and space.** The Python services took about 58 MB of RAM, and Python itself 22 MB on the system partition.
- **Two languages talking to each other.** A misspelled field on one side was only noticed when something went wrong. Once this made the player say "wrong password" for a Wi-Fi network that had failed for another reason.

In Beta 9.0 the whole platform is **Rust**, the language Reborn is written in. It's one program of 4.2 MB, with **no Python left on the player**. Every answer the platform gives is now run through Reborn's own reading code before a build is accepted, so a mismatch is caught before it reaches a player (letting the compiler check both sides directly is the next step).

### The numbers
Measured on the developer's player:

| | Beta 8.43 (Python) | Beta 9.0 (Rust) | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CPU the system services use while the player is on and idle | ≈ 92 s per hour | **≈ 12 s per hour** | about 7× less |
| CPU Reborn uses with the screen off and nothing playing | ≈ 45 s per hour | **≈ 14–16 s per hour** | about 3× less |
| Memory of the system services (counted per process) | 58 MB | **17 MB** | about 3½× less |
| Their real share of RAM (shared parts counted once) | 35 MB | **5.5 MB** | about 6× less |
| Answer to a simple question (sleep, update, battery state) | ≈ 0.5 s | **6–8 ms** | about 70× faster |
| System partition | 130 MB | **111 MB** | 19 MB more free space |
| Update download (system part) | 56.4 MB | **50.6 MB** | 6 MB smaller |
| Press Power → music player ready | ≈ 44 s | **≈ 37 s** | about 7 s faster |
| Shutdown steps after Power Off | ≈ 2.6 s | **≈ 1.2 s** | twice as fast |

What this means for you:
- **Less battery used while the player is on.** It matters most when the player sits on with the screen off: paused, or waiting to go to sleep.
- **Snappier system pages.** The battery, storage, update and Wi-Fi information no longer waits half a second per question.
- **A quicker start and shutdown**, more room on the system partition, and smaller updates.

Battery life *in sleep* is unchanged by this release (see Known issues).

### Reborn got leaner too
- **Quieter when dark.** With the screen off and nothing playing, Reborn now checks things every 5 seconds instead of every second, and reads the battery and storage every 10 seconds instead of every 2. A button press, music starting, a headset connecting or a computer being plugged in still wakes it at once.
- **No more sleep attempts on the charger.** The player can't sleep while a charger or computer is connected, but Reborn used to ask every minute anyway, and each try started a system process. Now it waits until the cable is unplugged; pressing Power still asks at once.

### How we made sure nothing broke
A rewrite like this touches the scariest parts of the system: running out of battery, sleep, and installing updates. So it went in careful steps:
1. **Recorded the old system first.** Every command and every file the platform uses was listed. The old Python platform was then recorded answering **1,069 test situations**: normal ones, odd ones and damaged files. It was also recorded handling **5,729 ways of typing its commands**.
2. **Translated without changing anything.** The Rust version had to give exactly the same answers, byte for byte, before Python was removed.
3. **Fixed what we found**, one fault at a time, each with its own test (list below).
4. **Turned it into proper Rust.** Every file the system keeps is now a clearly defined structure: the sleep record, the update journal, the SD card record, the shutdown request and about fifty more. The computer checks them instead of the code guessing what a field holds.
5. **Checked every step automatically:**
   - about 570 platform tests and 738 Reborn tests;
   - all recorded answers;
   - Reborn reading every platform answer;
   - a check that everything on your data partition stays readable by the previous version.

   That last check is what keeps **Restore Previous System** safe.
6. **22 test builds on a real player**, every one installed over the air and checked on the device.

### Fixes in this release
**Storage and USB**
- **The SD card goes back to read-only right after you unplug a computer.** While a computer was connected, the card's write permission was renewed every few seconds and never closed on unplug, so it stayed writable for up to 30 seconds.
- **A write permission that ran out could leave the card writable** until the next card was inserted or removed. The system now checks for that regularly.
- **SFTP** (file access for advanced users) opened the old music folder instead of Internal Storage.
- **A card with errors** (which plays read-only until repaired) was reported as a failure.

**Updates**
- **Two update checks at once** showed a confusing failure. Now: *"An update check is already running. Try again in a moment."*
- **Restore Previous System on a low battery** was refused but left the update page saying a restore was pending. The battery is now checked first.
- **Radio firmware that could not be installed** now shows as failed instead of looking like success.

**Battery, sleep and Wi-Fi**
- **DNS after an address renewal.** When the router renewed the player's address, Wi-Fi could show *no DNS* for up to five minutes. The DNS servers are now kept.
- **Battery percentage.** In one rare order of battery readings the power service stopped with an error and had to be restarted.

**Damaged files no longer cause internal errors.** A sudden power loss can damage one of the small records the system keeps. Now:
- the status pages stay readable, and the affected item shows as *unavailable*;
- sleep, updates and reset refuse with one clear reason and start a fresh record next time.

A damaged record never decides that something is safe.

### What did not change
- No new screens or settings, and nothing moved in the menus.
- The update installer and the recovery screen, both proven over many updates.
- The kernel (Linux 6.18) and drivers, apart from the version number.

The full story, written for players' owners, with a glossary and a technical appendix: **[Beta 9.0 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.0.md)**. Everything from Beta 8.43 is included.

- **Large SD cards play at once.** A card with tens of thousands of songs (over about 72 000 on a 1 TB card) was kept read-only and offered for a Repair that changed nothing. The card is now checked in the background while your music plays; only a card that really has errors asks for Repair.
- **Faster restarts with a big library:** after a restart the player no longer reads every unchanged folder again. If you edit tags on a computer, use Settings → **Scan for Music** afterwards.
- **Bluetooth headphones after a sleep:** pressing Play in the seconds before your headphones reconnect no longer plays on the speaker (or the empty jack). The player waits for them and plays there.
- **Wi-Fi:** no more "wrong password" when the password is right, and the player reconnects to your saved network by itself after a sleep or start, without tapping it.
- **Updates (#63):** an update that hung on "Installing Update" now restarts and finishes by itself, and the first start after an update no longer falls back to the rescue screen.
- **Restart and Power Off** can no longer hang with the screen dark (one player drained a full battery that way); if anything stalls, the player completes the restart or turns off by itself.
- **Battery:** the percentage stays right after a restart or update (it could show 13 % instead of 95 %), and the player now sleeps at low battery instead of staying awake and draining faster.
- **Holding Power right after waking** shows the power-off ring instead of cutting the power.
- **The screen at start:** a screen that stayed dark from power-on (seen once on an ST7701S player) is restarted by itself.
- **Error reports** now show more about why a player turned off, so the remaining cases can be found.

Everything from Beta 8.41 (internal speaker, headphone detection, haptic feedback) is included. Thanks for all the reports!

## Install (from stock)
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.8.42-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: the player sets up its Internal Storage (a few seconds), then Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

## Known issues (beta)
- Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on players with empty factory partitions (#62) use the chip's default calibration; please send a report if the range is poor.
- Some players turned off by themselves during playback; the cause is not found yet. If yours does, start it again and send a report.
- While a large SD card is being checked (up to a few minutes), you can't copy music to it over USB yet.
- The speaker uses the same volume as the headphones; its loudest step is the stock speaker's. Start low the first time.
- Going back to a version older than 8.33 starts with an empty queue (your settings are kept).
- Some car radios don't show the song and artist yet; we are looking into it.
- In a very long single-file book, jumping to another chapter takes 2–3 seconds.
- With very large libraries (100 000+ songs) a list can still take up to about a second the first time right after the player starts, and the first scan of such a card takes several minutes.
- Battery life in sleep: about 2 mA overnight on the developer's player (estimated from the battery voltage); stock is about 1.3 mA.
- BBC radio stations stream only in HLS, which the player does not play yet (planned for a later beta).
- FM radio is in the works for a later beta.
